title: Random example matrix output law
statement: Let $X=\{-1,1\}^n$, let $f:X\to\{-1,1\}$ be a target function, let $I$ be a finite index set, and let $m,w$ be natural numbers. Choose an array of inputs indexed by $I$ and $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ uniformly from all such arrays, label each input $x$ by $f(x)$, and apply a specified function to the resulting array. The output law is the distribution of the pair consisting of that function’s value and the cost $(|I|m,0,|I|m+w)$, recording random examples, membership queries, and local computation steps in that order.
hypotheses_covered: The target is a function from $\{-1,1\}^n$ to $\{-1,1\}$
The output function accepts arrays indexed by $I$ and $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ of input-label pairs
